description: AGSC-04-25 as added at rc.6. The content version is a pure function of two inputs a build already has — the git-log file of AGSC-08-20b and the build instant of AGSC-04-09 — so two engines given one repository derive one string. Derivation, case by case; the git-log file is oldest first and its last element is the built commit. (1) `tagged-head`: the built commit carries `tag: v2.0.0`, so branch 1 applies and the content version is that tag verbatim. (2) `untagged-head`: no tag on the built commit, the newest earlier tag is `v1.4.0` on element 1, there is 1 element after it up to and including the built commit, and the built commit's `sha` abbreviates to its first twelve characters `a1b2c3d4e5f6` — branch 2 gives `v1.4.0+1.ga1b2c3d4e5f6`. Twelve is fixed by the rule because git's own abbreviation length depends on the clone. (3) `no-tag-anywhere`: branch 3 counts the whole chain, three elements, giving `0.0.0+3.ga1b2c3d4e5f6`. (4) `no-git-history`: with no element at all, branch 4 renders the build instant, which AGSC-04-09 defaults to 0 with the warning AGSC-E606, as `19700101T000000Z` — AGSC-04-10's form with its separators removed, because `:` is outside the grammar `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._+-]{0,63}$` — giving `0.0.0+19700101T000000Z`. (5) `tag-outside-the-grammar`: `v2.0/final` is a legal git tag and not a legal content version, so the built commit is treated as untagged for this rule alone, the derivation falls to branch 2, and lint reports the value-was-defaulted warning AGSC-E506 naming the tag; the ledger is unaffected and still takes `kind: release` from that same tag (AGSC-08-20a). (6) `now-line`: the NOW line of AGSC-06-22 is the four values in the fixed order and with the fixed separators, the fingerprint being the bundle hash of AGSC-04-15, which this case states rather than derives — what is asserted here is the composition of the line, not the hash.
